description: §14.8.9 declassification — the RUNTIME half of item 4 (ss60-parked, adapter-gated). reveal("col") is the sole admit path: a server fn that returns u.reveal("passwordHash") declassifies that column at this value, so the E-ADAPTER server-eval roundtrip lands the FULL row on the client (@user = {id, name, passwordHash}). This is the client-visible PRESENCE counterpart to strip-client-visible-runtime's client-visible ABSENCE — proving reveal admits the named column past the sink at runtime, not just that it suppresses the compile-time gate.
rationale: §14.8.9 (SPEC.md E-PROTECT-004 row): 'the column is not reveal-declassified ... Resolution: declassify explicitly with value.reveal("col").' The reveal stamp on the row's provenance descriptor makes _scrml_protect_redact ADMIT passwordHash, so the client observes it present. Reveal admits the named column; it does not disarm the sink for the rest. ⚑ S441 (`g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar`): `I-PROTECT-STRIP-001` no longer co-fires here, because nothing is stripped — the info now fires only for a query whose row the egress sink ACTUALLY stripped (the §14.8.9 provenance flow, `compiler/src/codegen/protect-flow.ts`). Before S441 it fired for every protected SELECT, and this case pinned that false claim. Here every protected column of the row is revealed, so the sink strips nothing and the info must NOT fire.
